historicalEvidence.meaning: Owned same-SHA Rust binary/no ManualClock reproduced LAN first foreign-login and no-Origin health zero-byte stalls, while loopback worked; Python LAN TCP control worked. Only a 0.2-second service lsof LISTEN snapshot was taken, not continuous accept tracing. The precise cause was not established.

currentFrozenFailure.observed: Real LAN 192.168.3.96:61584 first foreign-Origin POST /lingxi/v1/web-auth/login stalled in write/read exchange with zero response bytes and failed after original twenty-second request budget. Test one target was 0 passed/1 failed; --no-fail-fast continues other targets.
currentFrozenFailure.doNotTreatPanicMessageAsDiagnosis: Existing panic text mentions firewall/TUN as possibility; that text is not causal evidence and cannot establish an environment root cause.

staticFindings.finding: Listener accept does not branch on peer being LAN versus loopback. Connection hard-cap exhaustion logs and drops socket immediately. Header-read timeout is Tokio wall time. No explicit twenty-second LAN wait path found.

With foreign Origin, origin-policy rejection is reached before connection classification, rate, auth and login handler. Interface enumeration is synchronous but the prior same-service loopback foreign-Origin control also completed; no evidence identifies it as this stall cause.

Default thirty-second request budget wraps downstream transport/auth/handler. A twenty-second zero-byte client timeout alone cannot prove the request never entered HTTP admission; it ends before the service default budget.
The failed first foreign-Origin request should not reach login. Credential auth is synchronous and password spawn_blocking is on a different branch; no evidence identifies either as the stall cause.

ManualClock is atomic timestamp input; fixed-window rate rejection is synchronous response, not waiting for the next window. Prior non-ManualClock reproduction already excludes freezing that clock as a necessary condition.

newReadOnlyObservations.result: Current route is interface lo0 with LOCAL/HOST flags. This is expected for this machine own address and does not show which program receives an accepted socket; self-address traffic is not a second-device/en0 path proof.
Help option rejected but usage explicitly supports -L/-a/-n and -p protocol. This was syntax/tool discovery, not a product/network test.

preconditions: Finish independent g receipts first and retain service failure unchanged.
Use the formally built g binary copied once to a dedicated isolated diagnostic directory; verify copy/build SHA match, source manifest and before/after bytes. No Cargo or product/test/tool edits.
Fresh empty home, production wall clock, LAN mode 0.0.0.0:0; only owned local sockets, no user account, secret credential or network configuration change.
Record exact own interface address and current route rather than assuming interface order; the diagnosis remains self-address, not actual mobile acceptance.
coreProcedure: Start one same-SHA owned service and capture stdout/stderr/READY, PID and actual bound port.

Make one raw no-Origin GET /lingxi/v1/health to its actual LAN self-address. Keep the original client deadlines: ten-second connect and twenty-second exchange. Record separate connect/write completion, client local/peer tuple, response-byte count and EOF/error. Do not add health credential.

While that exact socket remains open, collect a bounded timeline around 0.2/1/5/15 seconds: service-PID TCP FDs, client-PID TCP FDs, all sockets with this unique destination port, and listener qlen/incqlen/maxqlen. Record raw command output+timestamps, not only a conclusion.

During the same pending LAN request, perform one loopback no-Origin health control to the same PID/port with its exact socket tuple and HTTP bytes. This distinguishes a whole service stall from that path; it does not replace LAN acceptance.

If LAN health succeeds immediately, do one bounded foreign-Origin POST/login with a nonsecret dummy JSON value using the same monitoring. Expected403 is transport-only before auth, so no real credential is required. If health stalls, stop after its one window rather than repeat old login permutations.
Shut down the owned service through the existing signal, await the bounded shutdown, record exit/forced-cleanup fact and listener/PID gone; hash binary and raw evidence after run.
proposedSingleIsolation.outputHandling: Filter netstat snapshots to the one owned port and retain their headers. Never capture request bodies, user credentials or unrelated socket payload. Use subprocess argv, per-observer timeout, and keep the client deadline independent of observer runtime.

decisionTable.observed: Client connect/write complete; no matching server accepted FD; listener completed/incomplete queue rises
decisionTable.newInformation: Kernel-level listener queue contains this flow while application acceptance is not observed. Focus next on accept scheduling/readiness/ownership, not login/auth.

decisionTable.newInformation: Accepted socket reaches service. Focus next on Hyper request dispatch, body/header state or synchronous middleware rather than assuming preaccept filtering. A one-second read-only sample of the owned process may help locate a blocked worker; an async stack sample is diagnostic, not proof by itself.

Intermittency reproduced as current success only. Historical g and c failures remain failed and root cause unresolved; cannot relabel them pass.

proposedSingleIsolation.optionalFurtherMechanismOnlyIfNeeded: If socket timeline isolates an accepted HTTP-path question, a single owned Python TCP forwarder on actual LAN IP -> unchanged service loopback, preserving Host and foreign Origin, can test the actual same transport rejection code under another acceptor. Its peer address differs and it is not original LAN acceptance; do not substitute it for the failed gate.

limitations: No new service/probe/raw TCP listener or network test was executed by this reviewer. Only current route and netstat syntax were read.
No positive source-level cause is established. LISTEN-only lsof snapshot, zero bytes, panic wording, or an independent Python success cannot individually prove firewall/TUN or a Rust source defect.
